observation: agent-map exposes HybridSearch, SearchIndexStore, EmbeddingProvider and CorpusEmbeddingProvider::restore() publicly, but the only implementation that turns a SearchIndexStore back into the provider its vectors were written with is the private corpusProvider() method in AgentMapApplication, which reads the store meta keys embedding_state and embedding_fingerprint directly.

evidence.summary: private function corpusProvider(SearchIndexStore $store): ?CorpusEmbeddingProvider - reads meta(embedding_state) and meta(embedding_fingerprint) to rebuild the provider
agent-ui documents the deliberate omission and passes no EmbeddingProvider, so HybridSearch reports degraded_reason=semantic_channel_unavailable instead of the UI substituting a provider

hypothesis: A consumer that wants the semantic channel must therefore either reimplement that composition - putting a second copy of an owner vector-space contract, including its meta key names, into the consumer - or leave the channel off.
validated_conclusion: The semantic channel is unreachable from a consumer without crossing the owner boundary, so agent-ui leaves it off and renders agent-map's own semantic_channel_unavailable rather than reconstructing the provider. The smallest owner fix is a typed public factory on agent-map, for example CorpusEmbeddingProvider::restoredFrom(SearchIndexStore): ?self, used by the CLI as well so one implementation exists; the consumer constraint can then be bumped and the channel enabled.
